title: Authoring Reference — Training Segment Patterns
_comment: This file is a purpose-built reference that demonstrates every authoring principle. It is not a real training session. Use it to understand correct segment structure, label choices, and the meta vs transcript block distinction.

segments.title: Welcome & Session Overview
segments._comment: LECTURE type: trainer is speaking, no product on screen. Short intro passage merged into the overview rather than split — both form one continuous opening thought.

info.label: Opening Narration
info._comment: TRANSCRIPT BLOCK — has notes. Surfaces in transcript mode. Trainer can deliver from items alone (confident) or read notes verbatim (first-time/nervous).
items: Welcome everyone and thank you for joining
Introduce yourself and the session topic
Set time expectations for the session
Acknowledge that this is designed for all experience levels
notes:
### Welcome

Hello everyone, and welcome. Really glad you are here today.

My name is [Trainer Name] and over the next [X] hours we are going to cover [Topic]. This session is designed for all levels — whether you have never touched this before or you are already using it and want to go deeper, there is something here for you.

info.label: Module Outline
info._comment: META BLOCK — no notes. Items only. Describes slide content. Skipped by transcript mode — only visible at the planning/overview level.
items: Module 1: Core concepts and background
Module 2: Live product walkthrough
Module 3: Hands-on practice
Q&A at the end

info.label: Reaction Prompts
info._comment: META BLOCK — no notes. Prompts audience to use Teams React buttons. Convention for this session: 👍 = Yes, 😲 = No.
items: Have you used this product before? Thumbs up for yes, surprise for no!

segments.title: Core Concept: How It Works
segments._comment: LECTURE type. Two transcript blocks back to back: a brief Narration to set up the topic, then a deeper Concept Explanation. Followed by a meta Key Points block for the slide summary.

info.label: Narration
info._comment: TRANSCRIPT BLOCK — short setup narration. Sets context before the deeper explanation.
items: Before we look at the product, let's build the mental model
Understanding how this works under the hood makes everything else easier
Two key ideas: [Concept A] and [Concept B]
notes:
### Setting the Stage

Before I show you the interface, I want to spend a few minutes on the underlying concepts. Trust me — once you understand how this works, everything you see in the demo will make immediate sense.

info.label: Concept Explanation
info._comment: TRANSCRIPT BLOCK — the main conceptual explanation. Longer notes, multiple ### headings for sub-topics. This is the core of what transcript mode navigates through.
items: [Concept A]: what it is and why it matters
The limitation that [Concept A] creates on its own
[Concept B]: how it solves that limitation
Real-world analogy to make it concrete
notes:
### What Is [Concept A]?

[Concept A] is the engine behind the product. Think of it as a very sophisticated pattern-matching system trained on a huge amount of [relevant data]. It learns to recognise and generate [output type] that sounds natural and accurate.

Here is the catch though: it was trained on data up to a certain point in time. Ask it something from last week and it simply does not know.

### Solving the Gap with [Concept B]

That is exactly what [Concept B] is for. Instead of relying solely on the trained model, [Concept B] lets the product fetch fresh information from [source] and incorporate it into the response in real time.

A good analogy: the trained model is like a very well-read expert. [Concept B] is like handing that expert today's newspaper just before they answer your question.

info.label: Key Points
info._comment: META BLOCK — slide summary bullets. No notes. Skipped by transcript mode.
items: [Concept A] = trained on historical data, strong at natural language
[Concept B] = supplements the model with live or contextual data
Together: accurate, up-to-date, context-aware responses

segments.title: Live Interface Walkthrough
segments._comment: DEMO type: trainer is live in a product interface, clicking and navigating on screen. Three transcript blocks: Narration (sets up the demo), Demo Steps (the click-through), License Comparison (explains tier differences).

info.label: Narration
info._comment: TRANSCRIPT BLOCK — brief spoken lead-in before going live in the product.
items: Let's go live in the product now
URL / entry point to navigate to
Sign in required — needs an active account
notes:
### Into the Product

Alright, let's stop talking about it and actually go in. I am going to navigate to [URL] now — make a note of that, it is the most important thing to remember from today.

You will need to sign in with your [account type] account. If you are following along, do that now.

info.label: Demo Steps
info._comment: TRANSCRIPT BLOCK — narrates the live click-through. items = what to click, notes = what to say while clicking.
items: Show the main interface — point out the key areas
Open the [feature area] and explain each option
Show the [setting] toggle — explain what it controls
Run a sample interaction and explain the output
notes:
### Orienting to the Interface

This is the main screen. Across the top you have [navigation area]. On the left is [panel]. The centre is where [main action] happens.

### Trying It Live

I am going to type [sample input] here and show you what comes back. Watch the [specific element] — that tells you [what it means].

*[Run the interaction]*

See that? The product returned [description of output]. Notice it also pulled in [additional context] — that is [Concept B] in action, exactly what we just talked about.

info.label: License Comparison
info._comment: TRANSCRIPT BLOCK — explains feature differences between tiers. Notes walk through the comparison conversationally. Items give the scannable summary.
items: Tier 1 (included): [Feature set A] — web/public data only
Tier 2 (add-on): everything in Tier 1 + [Feature set B] — access to private/work data
Key unlock in Tier 2: [specific capability that requires the upgrade]
notes:
### Which Tier Do You Have?

Before you run off and try everything, let me be clear about what you have access to depending on your license.

**Tier 1 — included with [base product]:** You get [Feature set A]. The product can reach [public/web data source] to answer your questions. That is already very powerful.

**Tier 2 — the [add-on name]:** On top of that, you get [Feature set B], which means the product can now access [private/work data]. This also unlocks [specific capability].

If you are not sure which tier you have, [how to check]. The rest of today's demo works with Tier 1, so everyone can follow along.

segments.title: Hands-On Exercise
segments._comment: ACTIVITY type: participants are doing something themselves. Narration sets up the task; Slide Content lists the exercise steps as a meta block (participants can read the slide — no spoken script needed for the step list itself).

info.label: Narration
info._comment: TRANSCRIPT BLOCK — spoken setup for the exercise. Explains what to do and what success looks like.
items: Time for you to try it yourselves — five minutes
Goal: [what they should achieve by the end]
Work independently or with a neighbour
Drop your result in chat when done
notes:
### Your Turn

Alright, now it is your turn. I am going to give you about five minutes to try this yourself.

The goal is simple: [specific task description]. The steps are on the slide. When you have a result you are happy with, drop it in the **chat** — I want to see what everyone comes up with.

Work at your own pace. If you get stuck, Horan is watching the chat and will help you out.

info.label: Slide Content
info._comment: META BLOCK — the exercise steps as displayed on screen. No notes because participants read this themselves; the trainer does not narrate it line by line.
items: Step 1: Navigate to [URL] and sign in
Step 2: [Specific action]
Step 3: [Specific action]
Step 4: Review the output and note what surprised you
Share your result in the Teams chat

segments.title: Live Q&A
segments._comment: QA type: open Q&A exchange with live participant questions. One Narration block to open the floor. No pre-scripted content beyond the opener — Q&A is live and unscripted.

info.label: Narration
info._comment: TRANSCRIPT BLOCK — spoken transition into Q&A. Short opener to invite questions.
items: Open the floor — invite live questions now
Remind participants they can now unmute
Reference that chat questions are still welcome
Set a time boundary if needed
notes:
### Opening Q&A

Alright — that is the content for today. Well done everyone.

We have a few minutes now for live questions. If you have been holding something back, now is the time. Go ahead and **unmute** yourself and ask away. You can also keep posting in chat — Horan and I are both watching.

Who wants to go first?
